answer: Cross-epoch drift scoring. Each identity must keep its behavioral profile within a fixed distance of its own prior-epoch centroid, measured on features like timing, action mix, and counterpart diversity. Like sediment layering in a canyon, small drifts accumulate and are tolerated; abrupt shifts trigger revalidation. The prism of feature projection splits activity into independent axes so spoofing one axis alone fails. An attacker must sustain many identities across a glacier of epochs, paying continuous compute and coordination cost per identity rather than a one-time fee,
